$comment: Germany - Wave 5, and the architectural stress test for the whole pack
system. The EU is the hardest market and this pack is what proves the
design survives it WITHOUT a code change:
clinician_mode      -> false, and validate_packs.py FORBIDS true here
Why: MDR Annex VIII Rule 11 makes software intended for diagnosis,
prevention, monitoring, PREDICTION, prognosis or treatment a medical
device, and pushes most of it to Class IIa+ - Notified Body, ISO 13485,
IEC 62304, clinical evaluation. The 2025 revision of MDCG 2019-11 brought
prognosis/prediction software more explicitly into scope. Worse, Class IIa+
devices embedding AI are generally high-risk under the EU AI Act, so the
Same model, different words, different intended purpose. That is the whole
point of separating the pack from the code.

units_default.$note: Germany commonly uses mg/dL despite being metric elsewhere. Also expect ~35% string expansion vs English - no fixed-height buttons (PRD 13.2).

risk_model.$note: FINDRISC is European-derived and widely used in Germany, which helps the defensibility argument. But note it reports 10-year INCIDENCE - and a prediction claim is precisely what Rule 11 catches. The consumer-mode wording must stay on current metabolic health, not future prediction.

features.$hard_rule: clinician_mode_enabled MUST remain false in every EU pack without a Notified Body engagement. Enforced in validate_packs.py, not left to reviewer diligence.

regulatory.regime: EU MDR Annex VIII Rule 11 + EU AI Act
regulatory.gatekeeper: Notified Body (if device), GDPR Art. 9 for health data
regulatory.notes: Health data is special category under GDPR Art. 9: explicit consent, DPIA MANDATORY, EU residency, appointed representative, right to erasure, 72-hour breach notification. A Class IIa CE marking project is typically 12-24 months and six figures - treat the EU as a funded, scheduled programme, not a v1 checkbox. A Dec 2025 Commission proposal to amend Rule 11 is in progress but unsettled; do not plan on it landing.
